title: Outlook mobile: users choose whether meeting invitations stay in the inbox after they respond
notes: claim 15: severity blocker on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the briefing labels the setting user-opt-in and says only users who change it notice anything, although its initial state is not documented. The statement that no meter applies also goes beyond the evidence. The roadmap facts, general app licensing and PowerShell syntax are supported.

claims.claim: Outlook mobile users can choose whether invitations are automatically removed from their inbox after responding.
claims.quote: You can now control whether meeting invitations are automatically removed from your inbox after you RSVP.

claims.claim: The user setting is Settings > Calendar > Delete Invite After RSVP, which can be turned off or on.
claims.quote: Simply to go to settings, calendar, and turn off or on "Delete Invite After RSVP."

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this mobile feature; its specific behaviour rests on the roadmap.
claims.quote: Searched: "Delete Invite After RSVP" "Outlook"; Outlook mobile "Delete Invite After RSVP" default on off Deleted Items. Opened Outlook mobile FAQ, app configuration and Set-MailboxCalendarConfiguration; no feature description found.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the mobile toggle starts on or off.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile "Delete Invite After RSVP" default on off Deleted Items; "Delete Invite After RSVP" "Outlook". Opened Outlook mobile FAQ, app configuration and cmdlet reference; neither these nor the roadmap gives the mobile default.

claims.claim: The defaultState value user-opt-in accurately describes this new control's state on arrival.
claims.quote: defaultState: "user-opt-in"; "Microsoft has not stated whether the toggle starts on or off, so it is not known whether existing mobile users will see a change ... before they touch it."
claims.fix: Set defaultState to "unknown". For a feature that is itself a new control, the standard requires unknown when its initial state is not stated; the existence of a personal choice and absence of an admin switch do not establish its initial behaviour.

claims.claim: Only mobile users who open Settings and change the toggle notice anything.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile "Delete Invite After RSVP" default on off Deleted Items; "Delete Invite After RSVP" "Outlook". Opened Outlook mobile FAQ, app configuration and cmdlet reference; no source establishes unchanged behaviour for users who do nothing.
claims.fix: Replace the impact rationale with: "Low. This is a personal invitation-handling control in Outlook mobile; Microsoft has not stated its starting value or whether existing behaviour changes for users who leave it alone."

claims.where: controls[0].ui; controls[0].api; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no admin default or lock for Outlook mobile's Delete Invite After RSVP toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook iOS Android Delete Invite After RSVP Intune app configuration admin lock default Exchange PowerShell. Opened Outlook app configuration and Set-MailboxCalendarConfiguration; no documented mobile preset or lock found.

claims.claim: The documented general app configuration settings contain no meeting-invitation setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook iOS Android Delete Invite After RSVP Intune app configuration admin lock default Exchange PowerShell. Read the app configuration settings table and searched the full page for invitation, RSVP, DeleteMeetingRequest and meeting; no invitation-handling key found.

claims.claim: Outlook mobile general app settings can be delivered through Intune or another UEM provider.
claims.quote: This capability is offered for both enrolled devices via any UEM provider and for devices that aren't enrolled when Outlook for iOS and Android has an Intune App Protection Policy applied.

claims.claim: The general app configuration table includes Focused Inbox, Sync Calendars, Block external images and Default Font.
claims.quote: | Focused Inbox | On |; | Sync Calendars | Off |; | Block external images | Load for Safe Senders only (value 1) |; | Default Font | Off |

claims.claim: Exchange PowerShell documents Set-MailboxCalendarConfiguration -Identity <MailboxIdParameter> -DeleteMeetingRequestOnRespond $false as a call setting the named Boolean mailbox parameter.
claims.quote:
Set-MailboxCalendarConfiguration
    [-Identity] <MailboxIdParameter>
    ...
    [-DeleteMeetingRequestOnRespond <Boolean>]

claims.claim: DeleteMeetingRequestOnRespond is available only in Exchange Online.
claims.quote:
### -DeleteMeetingRequestOnRespond

> Applicable: Exchange Online

This parameter is available only in the cloud-based service.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature reaches no new data and acts on nothing beyond the user's mailbox.
claims.quote: Searched: "Delete Invite After RSVP" "Outlook". Opened Outlook mobile FAQ, app configuration and cmdlet reference. The roadmap describes inbox invitation handling but does not establish exhaustive data access or processing boundaries for this feature.
claims.fix: Replace the Data exposure bullet with "The roadmap describes a control over invitation emails in the user's inbox." Replace the risk rationale with "Low. The documented change is a personal control over whether invitation emails stay in the inbox after a response."

claims.claim: No new sign-in, permission or connection is described for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "Delete Invite After RSVP" "Outlook". Read roadmap and opened Outlook mobile FAQ, app configuration and Set-MailboxCalendarConfiguration; no new sign-in, permission or connection described for this feature.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not describe whether this mobile toggle moves invitation emails to Deleted Items or removes them another way.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile "Delete Invite After RSVP" default on off Deleted Items. Opened mobile FAQ, app configuration and cmdlet reference; no mobile disposal mechanism stated. EWS and desktop MeetingItem deletion references do not identify this toggle's implementation.

claims.claim: No source says existing invitation-handling behaviour changes for users who leave the toggle alone.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook mobile "Delete Invite After RSVP" default on off Deleted Items; "Delete Invite After RSVP" "Outlook". Opened mobile FAQ, app configuration and cmdlet reference; no source states whether behaviour changes for untouched settings.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every control the checklist tells readers to check appears in the controls table.
claims.quote: "Check on a test device whether the toggle starts on or off"; the table contains "Admin default or lock" and "Mailbox calendar parameter DeleteMeetingRequestOnRespond", not the personal Delete Invite After RSVP control.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet "Check on a test device whether the toggle starts on or off, so helpdesk guidance matches what users see." It asks readers to check a personal control not represented in the table; do not add a control row as part of this correction.
